Floating-point addition is not associative because the finite precision of the mantissa forces intermediate results to be rounded to the nearest representable value. For example, adding a very small number to a very large number can completely lose the small number due to rounding, whereas adding the small numbers together first preserves their sum before combining with the large number. Consequently, different groupings of the same operands produce different intermediate roundings, leading to different final results.
